NONE: › an object worn because it is believed to protect against evil, disease, or unhappiness
B2 to entertain someone, especially by humorous speech or action or by making them laugh or smile
（尤指透過幽默的言行）逗樂，逗笑；給…提供消遣（或娛樂）
B2 to keep someone happy, especially for a short time

example: I've brought an article from yesterday's paper that I thought might amuse you.
我帶來了昨天報上的一篇文章，或許可以讓你開懷一笑。
[ + obj + to infinitive ] I think it amuses him to see people make fools of themselves.
我想他看到這些人裝瘋賣傻的樣子肯定會覺得好玩。
Apparently these stories are meant to amuse.
顯然這些故事的目的就在於搞笑。
We amused ourselves by watching the passers-by.
我們看著來往的行人自得其樂。
Shall I put on a DVD to amuse the kids?
要不要給孩子放段影片，逗他們開心？

NONE: B2 showing that you think something is funny
B2 to keep someone interested and help them to have an enjoyable time
使（某人）快樂；給（某人）消遣

example: an amused smile
開心的微笑
She was very amused by/at your comments.
她被你的話逗得很開心。
Toddlers don't need expensive toys and games to keep them amused.
蹣跚學步的幼兒不需要甚麼昂貴的玩具和高檔的消遣就能夠玩得很開心。

U: B2 [ U ] the feeling of being entertained or made to laugh

C: B2 [ C ] an activity that you can take part in for entertainment

example: She looked at him with amusement.
她忍俊不禁地看著他。
I looked on in amusement as they started to argue.
他們開始爭吵起來，我在旁邊高興地看熱鬧。
Carl came last in the race, (much) to my amusement.
卡爾比賽得了個倒數第一，（真）把我給樂壞了。
I play the piano just for my own amusement (= to entertain myself, not other people).
我彈鋼琴純粹是自娛自樂。
There was a range of fairground amusements, including rides, stalls, and competitions.
在露天遊樂場有很多好玩的，可以騎馬、逛貨攤以及參加比賽。

NONE: › a place in which you can pay to play games on machines
（有電子遊戲機之類娛樂設施的）遊樂場；遊戲機廳
好笑的，有趣的；引人發笑的

example: an amusing story/person/situation
有趣的故事／風趣的人／好笑的場面
